Definition: Total media investment in the selected period, excluding agency fees and production.
Why it matters: The denominator for every efficiency ratio. Without a clean spend number, CAC, ROAS and MER cannot be compared across channels or periods.
Source / owner: Ad platforms reconciled to finance; Marketing Ops

Definition: Year-one membership revenue attributed to the paid channel of first touch.
Why it matters: Connects media activity to the only outcome that matters. Should be reconciled to CRM and finance, not ad-platform revenue.

Definition: Average media cost to acquire one paying member across all paid channels.
Why it matters: The headline viability metric. Rising blended CAC with flat AOV means the growth engine is degrading, even if lead volume is up.

Definition: Revenue generated per dollar of total media spend, including channels that receive no last-click credit.
Why it matters: A robust, attribution-light efficiency check. Harder to game than platform ROAS and useful for board-level reporting.

Definition: Attributed revenue divided by spend for a channel or campaign.
Why it matters: Useful for relative channel comparison and creative triage, but it is not incremental and should never be the sole budget authority.

Definition: Expected lifetime gross revenue from a member, modelled from observed cohorts.
Formula: First-year AOV x LTV multiple (2.2x sample)
Why it matters: High-ticket businesses can rationally pay more than first-year revenue for a member. Using LTV rather than AOV prevents under-investing in quality channels.

Definition: Lifetime value per member relative to the cost of acquiring one.
Why it matters: The core unit-economics test. Below roughly 3:1 the business cannot fund growth, overheads and margin comfortably; above 5:1 it may be under-investing.

Definition: Months of revenue needed to recover the cost of acquiring a member.
Why it matters: Cash-flow guardrail. Even with strong LTV, slow payback constrains how fast the business can scale spend.

Definition: Number of ad impressions served.
Why it matters: Top-of-funnel volume and the denominator for CPM and CTR. Falling impressions at rising spend signals auction pressure or audience saturation.
Target / guardrail: Monitor vs spend; no hard target

Definition: Cost per 1,000 impressions.
Why it matters: Measures the cost of attention. A rising CPM alongside falling CTR is the classic creative-fatigue and audience-saturation signature.

Definition: Clicks divided by impressions.
Why it matters: The first test of message-market fit. CTR declines are an early warning that creative or audience is tiring before CAC visibly moves.

Definition: Average cost per click.
Why it matters: Combines auction cost and creative resonance. Useful for diagnosing whether a CAC increase comes from media costs or landing-page conversion.
Target / guardrail: Monitor; alert on +20% week on week

Definition: Share of ad clicks that successfully load the landing page.
Why it matters: Detects broken links, slow pages and tracking loss. A drop here wastes paid clicks before the funnel even starts.

Definition: Share of landing-page sessions that register for a masterclass or equivalent lead offer.
Why it matters: Measures landing-page and offer conversion. It is the lever that changes CPL without changing media buying.

Definition: Media cost per masterclass registration or gated-asset lead.
Why it matters: The first purchasable unit of the funnel. Must always be read with lead quality: cheap leads that never book calls destroy value.

Definition: Share of registrants who attend live or consume the replay within the attribution window.
Why it matters: The largest controllable leak in a webinar-led model. Registration without attendance produces no sales conversations and inflates apparent CPL.

Definition: Share of attendees who meet the qualified-lead definition (budget, intent, location, investable capacity).
Why it matters: Separates education-hungry traffic from prospects the sales team can actually serve. Low MQL rate means the promise and the qualification criteria are misaligned.

Definition: Media cost per marketing-qualified lead.
Why it matters: A better optimisation target than CPL because it rewards lead quality rather than raw volume.

Definition: Share of MQLs that book a strategy call.
Why it matters: Measures the handoff from marketing to sales and the strength of the call offer. A weak booking rate is usually a follow-up speed and messaging problem, not a media problem.

Definition: Media cost per strategy call booked.
Why it matters: The most actionable mid-funnel efficiency metric. Lets marketing be judged on conversations created rather than forms completed.
Source / owner: Ad platforms + CRM; Head of Growth

Definition: Share of booked calls where the prospect attends.
Why it matters: No-shows are pure wasted acquisition cost. Reminder sequences and qualification reduce cost per member without touching media.

Definition: Share of masterclass leads that become paying members.
Why it matters: The end-to-end quality check. It prevents celebrating cheap leads that never convert and exposes segment-specific nurture gaps.

Definition: Share of held calls that close into membership.
Why it matters: Primarily a sales-quality and offer-fit metric. Falling close rates on stable call volume points to lead quality or sales enablement issues.

Definition: CAC, lead-to-member rate and AOV broken out by first-time investor, experienced investor and retiree.
Formula: Segment spend / segment members; segment members / segment leads
Why it matters: Blended averages hide cross-subsidy. A segment can look acceptable in total while quietly destroying value or being starved of budget.

Definition: Mean elapsed days between first lead touch and membership close.
Formula: AVG(member close date - first touch date)
Why it matters: Sets the correct evaluation window for campaigns. Judging long-cycle channels on 7-day ROAS systematically kills the channels that create the best members.
Target / guardrail: Use p90 as the attribution window

Definition: Time from lead creation to first attempted human contact, reported in buckets.
Formula: First contact timestamp - lead created timestamp
Why it matters: One of the highest-leverage variables in high-ticket lead gen. Fast response materially increases booking and show rates at zero media cost.

Definition: Share of video impressions that hold for at least three seconds.
Why it matters: Diagnoses the opening frame. Weak hook rate means the ad never earns attention, regardless of how good the offer is.

Definition: Share of viewers who reach the key offer or completion point.
Why it matters: Measures whether the long-form asset actually sells. Retention curves show exactly where prospects drop out and what to re-cut.

Definition: Change in CTR and CPM over a rolling 14-day window at stable frequency.
Why it matters: Caught early, fatigue can be fixed by rotation; caught late, it shows up as an unexplained CAC increase and wasted spend.

Definition: Revenue caused by the campaign, measured against a holdout or lift test, divided by spend.
Why it matters: The only way to know whether paid media creates revenue or takes credit for demand that would have converted anyway. Essential for brand and retargeting.

Definition: Share of CRM member events successfully matched back to ad-platform identities.
Formula: Matched offline conversions / total offline conversions
Why it matters: If match rates are low, platforms optimise on incomplete signals and CAC reporting is wrong. This is the health check for the measurement foundation.
Source / owner: Meta CAPI / Google enhanced conversions; Marketing Ops

Definition: Model-predicted probability that a lead becomes a member, plus top-decile vs bottom-decile conversion.
Formula: Model score (AUC); top-decile conversion / average conversion
Why it matters: Lets sales prioritise the right leads and lets ad platforms optimise toward likely members rather than cheap form fills.

Definition: Actual spend versus planned spend for the period.
Why it matters: Prevents end-of-month panic spending and protects learning phases. Pacing variance also confounds week-on-week CAC comparisons.
